county_early_notes: ev_2026: Texas SOS daily Early Voting Turnout report (in-person + mail ballots received) through Oct 30, 2026 (final day of early voting), as republished by TexPolls (all 254 counties; value_source=sos for every county). The SOS site itself (earlyvoting.sos.state.tx.us) was unreachable from this environment (proxy CONNECT 502), so the TexPolls mirror of the SOS report is the primary source.

ev_2024: DERIVED = theoelections 2026 county total / its 'vs 2024' ratio (theoelections compares 2026 early vote to the county's final 2024 general early vote). Derived, rounded. Validated against Chris Tackett's published final 2024 county early-vote totals (Harris 1,229,926 vs derived 1,230,388; Dallas 659,302 vs 659,216; Tarrant 658,484 vs 658,442; Bexar 603,220 vs 603,105; Travis 481,643 vs 481,236; Collin 435,403 vs 435,666): all within 0.1%. Statewide sum 9,042,332 (~9.0M, matches SOS-reported 2024 early vote). Null where theoelections had no matching county (none).

ev_2022: not obtained at county level (SOS 2022 archive report blocked: earlyvoting.sos.state.tx.us 502 via proxy, sos.state.tx.us/elections/earlyvoting/2022/nov8.shtml 403). Instead inperson_turnout_pct_2022_final = TexPolls' 2022 in-person early-vote turnout (% of 2022 registered) for the same (final) day, from SOS archives; compare with turnout_pct_2026 (which includes mail).
theo_ev_2026 (theoelections) runs slightly above the SOS figure because theoelections substitutes higher county-office counts; statewide 7,744,549 vs SOS 7,711,462.

primary_history.method_note: Two different methods. (a) Derek Ryan / Ryan Data & Research: classifies each early voter by the party primary they MOST RECENTLY voted in (so a voter who switched to the 2026 Dem primary counts as D). (b) theoelections voter-file match: 'Democratic primaries only' / 'Republican primaries only' / 'both parties' / 'no primary' over the voter's primary history. Method (a) shows a small D edge; method (b) a small R-only edge with 39% no-primary. Neither is vote choice.

2026.source: theoelections.com/early-vote (voter-file match): in person 7,463,553 = D-only 2,100,396 (28.1%), R-only 2,238,247 (30.0%), both 185,982 (2.5%), none 2,938,928 (39.4%); by mail 280,996 = D-only 92,275 (32.8%), R-only 73,688 (26.2%), both 5,908 (2.1%), none 109,125 (38.8%). Combined above.

ryan.final: Democrats finished the final day of early voting with a ~26,000-vote edge, based on which party's primary voters most recently participated in (Derek Ryan, via Texas Tribune 2026-11-03). Republicans had advantages of 945,000 in 2024 and 565,000 in 2022 on the same basis.

through_day7.source: Texas Tribune 2026-10-27 citing Ryan: D-primary history 35% of ballots, R 33%, 29% never voted / general-only, 4% mixed

through_day5.source: Houston Public Media / KSAT citing Ryan; D edge ~75,000 statewide through Oct 23

ryan.remaining_pool: Ryan: >2.1M Texans who voted in at least one of the last four GOP primaries had not yet voted by end of EV; ~2.7M non-voters considered likely to still vote (Tribune 2026-11-03).

2026.models: Ross Hunt (R pollster) model of the early electorate: 53.3% D / 46.7% R; a Democratic-built model: 50.5% D / 49.5% R (Texas Tribune 2026-11-03).

2022.source: Derek Ryan final-week 2022 report as quoted by Fox 4 / sicem365 repost: R-primary history 40%, D-primary 29%, no primary history 30% ('first time no-history share exceeds D share'). Through day 10 (4,227,631 ballots): 43% R / 31% D / 27% none (Ryan via KXAN/Spectrum, 2022-11-03). Tribune 2026-11-03: R advantage 565,000 on most-recent-primary basis.
2022.caveat: secondary quotations of Ryan's PDF; exact final-day figures not retrieved

2024.source: Derek Ryan via Texas Tribune / ABC13 (Nov 2024): 2.5 million early voters had previously voted in a Republican primary vs 1.6 million in a Democratic primary (~28% R / ~18% D of ~9.0M); about a quarter of the early vote had no partisan-primary history (same as 2020). Tribune 2026-11-03: R advantage 945,000 in 2024 on most-recent-primary basis.
2024.caveat: category definitions in the 2024 quotes do not sum to 100%; final Ryan 2024 shares not retrieved

2026_ryan.basis: Derek Ryan 'most recent primary' classification; final shares ESTIMATED from his day-7 shares (35/33/29+4) and the final ~26k D edge (Texas Tribune 2026-11-03)

2022_ryan.basis: Ryan final-week 2022 report (R 40 / D 29 / none 30, +~1 mixed)

2024_ryan.basis: Ryan: R advantage 945,000 in 2024 early vote (Texas Tribune 2026-11-03); party shares not found

early_vote_margin_models_2026.note: estimated D-R vote margin of the 2026 early electorate: Ross Hunt (R) 53.3-46.7, a Democratic model 50.5-49.5 (Texas Tribune 2026-11-03)

eday_live.note: No county publishes a machine-readable Election Day check-in feed that is reachable from here; figures below are from press conferences / social posts relayed by local media. theoelections.com has a 'hour by hour, today' module (data/live/hourly.json) but its data files return HTTP 403 (bot check; not circumvented). Dallas, Bexar, Travis, Tarrant, Collin: no Election Day totals found in accessible sources yet.

eday_2026.note: 'over 88,000' - Clerk Teneshia Hudspeth press conference (ABC13 live blog)
'more than 100,000 in-person votes cast on Election Day' - Harris County Elections social post (ABC13 / Houston Chronicle)
'more than 143,000 votes cast today' - Houston Chronicle live blog; county passed 1.2M total votes incl. early (midterm record)

48201.read: Harris ED pace at 1:15pm (143k) is ~93% of the 2024 presidential pace at 1pm (153.5k) - very high for a midterm; early vote was 87.8% of 2024.

statewide.ev_2026_as_of: 2026-10-30 (final day of early voting; SOS unofficial daily report, mail ballots received through Oct 30)

ev_2026_alt.texas_tribune: more than 7.7 million (40.5% of registered), SOS preliminary as of Sun Nov 1

statewide.ev_2022_note: approx: Texas Tribune '5.5 million voted early in 2022, 31% of registered'; Dallas Morning News '5.4 million, 31% of 17.7M'; 31% x 17,672,143 = 5.48M. SOS county-level 2022 archive not reachable.
statewide.ev_2024_note: sum of derived county ev_2024 (theoelections 2026/vs-2024 ratios); consistent with Texas Tribune '9 million cast early ballots in 2024, 49%' and Chris Tackett '8.88 million'; Fox 7 in-person only 8,708,659.
statewide.registered_2026_note: sum of SOS county registration used in the Oct 30 report (TexPolls reference file, registered_through_date 2026-10-30); Texas Tribune: 'more than 19 million, up 2.2% from Nov 2024'
notes: Early-vote turnout 40.5% of registered: highest midterm early vote in modern TX history (beats 2018). 2022 was 31%; 2024 (presidential) 49%.
If 2026 early vote is ~68% of the total (the 2022 share), total turnout ~11.3M; at the 2024 share (79%) ~9.7M. Mark Jones (Rice) and Derek Ryan floated ~10M total.
Texas has no party registration: partisan reads below are from primary-voting history (imperfect; Ryan's own caveat) or from county geography.
SOS registration/turnout page (sos.state.tx.us/elections/historical/70-92.shtml) gives totals only, no early/ED split.
